sourceNotes.issue: The AD520 attestation dates Yuan Xi’s letter, not Lu Ji’s historical death allusion; identity merge is supported by 昔/華亭鶴唳. Date qualification is not approved here.
English Lu Ji courtesy alias points to 士龍/Lu Yun, not 士衡/Lu Ji. Keep separate.
Source treatise has internally inconsistent usurpation date order. Named prince and repeated events remain identifiable; this review does not repair or approve chronology.
Extracted parent-of 璪 is not supported as a direct son by 臣高祖…璪，囗之嫡孫. This is a genealogical claim issue; retrospective grand-guardian identity is explicit.
Several office labels are clauses (倫使人持出/倫使更求/謂倫留將服其罪也), not offices; these are extraction claim defects, not proof of mixed identity.
Historicity claim c0877 cites s0014 about 袁躍 rather than 陸機. The name/literary identity in s0008 remains explicit.
Liu Song polity hint conflicts with Nong Zhigao/Guangzhou Northern Song context; written surname 魏 separately distinguishes the endpoint.

decisions.basis: 陸機大墓賦 introduces a named literary quotation in commentary; the preceding Cao Cao military date does not date the quoted author.
陸機 commands Sima Ying’s forces toward the capital and is defeated at 建春門: the same distinctive final campaign as the Lu Ji/Chengdu episode.
陸覬 privately reassures Northern Wei nobles in Xiaowen’s court; different written given name and later dynastic setting.
績、蕃舊器 refers back to 陸績 and 王蕃 astronomical instruments in the same treatise; not Lu Ji the Jin writer.
陸機為譚傳曰 names the author of the quoted Gu Tan biography, not an officer participating in the Wu events being quoted.
路季 is enfeoffed 小黃公 among Sima Jiong’s meritorious followers; distinct written personal name from 陸機.
潘、陸之華 is the conventional pair of Jin literary models in Kong Huan’s criticism of Jiang Zong; it is a retrospective allusion, not Lu Yu himself.
黃門郎陸機 is arrested after 趙王倫 fails, matching the poet’s Western Jin court service and the Tongjian 殿中郎陸機 appointment under Lun.
陸績 is Gu Shao’s maternal uncle and contemporary of Lu Xun in Sun Quan’s court; the written given name and generation differ from 陸機.
陸機所以賦豪士也 names the author of 豪士 in the historian’s literary-moral example.
陸機 is Ying’s vanguard commander against Changsha, a compatriot of Sun Hui, executed with his brothers; the parallel Sanguozhi passage explicitly names 雲、耽.
陸機 is Ying’s vanguard commander and killed with brothers 雲、耽 in Sun Hui’s embedded biography; directly matches Jinshu071.
潘、陸之華 in the Kong Huan/Jiang Zong episode is parallel to Chenshu021, a conventional literary comparison with Pan Yue and Lu Ji.
顧榮、陸機、陸雲 jointly recommend He Xun after Wu’s fall; full name plus brother and Jin-service episode bridge the writer.
吾家平原詣張壯武 retrospectively recalls Lu Pingyuan visiting Zhang Hua; the clan and Pingyuan designation bridge to 晉平原內史陸機.
陸機爲太康之英 explicitly places the named poet among Anren and Jingyang in the Taikang literary revival.
Explicit 晉惠帝太安二年 Chengdu Ying, Lu Ji’s capital campaign, defeat and execution match Jinshu004/071.
昔…陸機想華亭鶴唳 is explicitly a historical death allusion in Yuan Xi’s last letter; AD520 describes the quoting speaker, not Lu Ji.
The annotation explicitly places 陆机 as 成都王大都督 recruiting Sun Cheng, then both killed; the era wording 永安 does not create a second Lu Ji.
陸機《豪士》 explicitly identifies the historical author of the work used to assess Liu Zhiji’s rhapsody.
士衡所雲「同川而異歸」 is a quoted literary maxim by Shiheng, the same courtesy-name author as root Nanqishu035.
晉平原內史陸機 is expressly the brother-in-law of Gu Qian; the Pingyuan office bridges the historical Jin writer.
殿中郎陸機 becomes 相國倫’s 參軍 among famous recruited men, matching Jinshu047’s courtier after Lun’s fall.
陸興言於世網 is a surname-only literary allusion. It fits Lu Ji’s literary setting but the sealed passage gives no full name or independent family/office bridge; preserve uncertainty.
士衡 is paired with 安仁 as a poetic model, exactly paralleling the root’s already-merged Nanqishu035 courtesy-name citation.
陸士衡 is paired with 曹元首 in the historical debate on enfeoffment; full surname plus courtesy name identifies Lu Ji, not a Tang actor.
漢末吳人陸績, the astronomer who built 渾象, has distinct written name and early Wu career.
詠陸機吊魏武 introduces Lu Ji’s elegy quoted by Qiang; the ensuing death narrative is Qiang’s, not a later Lu Ji.
The complete paragraph concerns compilation of 晉書 and the emperor’s four historical critiques, including 陸機; this names the Jin biographical/literary subject.
Yu Zhong recognized 吳郡陸機 when he was a child and he later became renowned; the Wu youth episode fits the Jin writer and is explicitly different from following 陸績字公紀.
陸績 commentator on 揚玄 and official in 南越 is the Gongji/Yulin scholar, distinct written given name and career.
卿之士龍 addresses Wang Li about his brother Ji by comparison with Lu Yun’s courtesy name Shilong; Lu Ji’s courtesy is 士衡. The English alias Lu Ji is wrong.
盧璣字正甫, son of 盧彥倫, serves Jin Zhangzong and dies 泰和六年 at eighty: different written name, family and dynasty.
陸績字公紀, son of Lu Kang, hides oranges for his mother before Yuan Shu, serves Sun Quan and dies thirty-two; distinct from 陸機/士衡.
征東大將軍衛瓘 takes 青州 command; the later annal explicitly transfers this same officeholder to northern command.
鎮北大將軍衛瓘 becomes 菑陽公 in Jin’s founding appointments, same name and distinguished northern military career.
晉征北將軍衛瓘 asks to retain Shamo Han and bribe tribal leaders, parallel to Weishu001 and the Jin northern command.
魏觀 serves in Ming founding institutions (diarist, ritual adviser or 國學祭酒); different written name and dynasty from Western Jin 衛瓘.
司空衛瓘 memorializes restoration of local selection under Wudi, same named Minister of Works in the root.
The emperor continues 衛瓘’s 論語 annotation; this is a preexisting named author retrospectively referenced, compatible with the learned Jin statesman.
Rejected marriage of 衛公女, tutor 衛瓘’s criticism, and Jia’s use of Wei to kill him and Liang connect one named statesman.

監軍衛瓘 helps kill Zhong Hui during the Shu revolt; matches the root’s Wei264 military endpoint and later 伐蜀 merit.
太保衛瓘 recruits Liu Shen before Jiong’s later regency, matching the Western Jin grand guardian and chronology.
The historian criticizes Wuyuan Yang for blocking 衛瓘’s words and accepting Zhang Hong’s deception, the heir’s competence test in Jinshu031.
晉征北將軍衞瓘 detains Shamo Han and bribes chiefs; full paragraph explicitly identifies his Jin office and matches Beishi001.
尚書令衛瓘 becomes 司空, bridging the northern commander/secretariat director to the root’s Minister of Works.
敻子瓘 is Wei Xiong’s son and acting Sui governor, dying alongside news of Xiaokuan’s son; a different family and Northern Zhou generation.
